solution.answer: Insufficient validated artifact content to produce a confident integrated answer. The only artifact supplied (signed_interaction_lattice) was a preliminary pass with no findings, no simulation run, and no distinguishing observations verified. It asserts only that the minimal architecture has at least 3 edges. Based solely on that translated content: the smallest signed causal architecture is a 3-edge incoherent feed-forward loop (ligand->Y activating, ligand->Z activating, Z-|Y repressing), where Z is transcriptionally induced and represses Y, producing transient Y that adapts. However, the discriminating observations, the Z_KO minute-8 prediction, and the second-pulse prediction depend on the numerical time-course fit that was never completed, and the two domains that would have supplied mechanism-discrimination and relaxation kinetics produced no artifact. Therefore these parts of the question cannot be answered from validated content.

domain_contributions.signed_interaction_lattice: Preliminary pass only; no simulation run and no findings. Contributes solely the structural constraint that the minimal explanatory architecture requires at least 3 signed edges, consistent with an incoherent feed-forward loop (ligand->Y, ligand->Z, Z-|Y). No numerical fit, distinguishing observations, Z_KO prediction, or second-pulse prediction were verified.

gaps: Numerical fit to observations.csv was never verified, so the specific signed architecture cannot be confirmed beyond the >=3-edge constraint.
No artifact identifies which observations distinguish incoherent feed-forward from Y-dependent negative feedback or receptor desensitization (mechanism_discriminant_measures produced nothing).
No artifact provides the minute-8 Y prediction for Z_KO; relaxation_kinetics_field, which would model this, produced nothing.
No validated basis for predicting whether a second ligand pulse after washout is weaker, similar, or stronger, since this depends on unmeasured recovery/relaxation kinetics.
